title: Water Resources, Irrigation Projects and River Linking
intake_rule: Every rendered page was read visually once before note or MCQ authoring. Printed prose, tables, boxes, maps, diagrams and PYQs were indexed; handwritten marks were ignored.
table_rule: Every printed table is preserved cell-by-cell in a responsive semantic table. Verified corrections and dated enrichment are labelled separately and never silently replace the printed source cell.

pages.source_heading: India water-resources statistics, irrigation-project classes and dam types

facts.claim: A medium project has a CCA from 2,000 to 10,000 hectares. A CCA of 7,500 hectares falls within this interval.
A gravity dam relies mainly on the weight of its concrete or masonry body; an arch dam transfers load to abutments.

The table gives 328.76 million hectares as geographical area and 141.71 million hectares as net sown area. Gross irrigated area is 122.29 million hectares and reporting area is 306.65 million hectares.
Drip and sprinkler are water-application methods. Major, medium and minor are CCA-based project classes.

pages.source_heading: Global water distribution and Bhakra-Nangal project

facts.claim: Bhakra is a 225.55-m concrete straight-gravity dam on the Sutlej and impounds Gobind Sagar. Downstream Nangal Dam diverts Sutlej water into the canal network.
The printed table gives 97.20% for oceans/saline lakes, 2.15% for ice/glaciers and 0.64% for groundwater. These are rounded historical values; all-water and freshwater denominators must not be mixed.
The all-water table assigns 97.20% to oceans and saline lakes; 93.37% belongs to a different freshwater denominator.

pages.source_heading: Beas project and Damodar Valley Corporation

facts.claim: BBMB identifies Unit-I as the Beas–Sutlej Link diverting Beas water at Pandoh toward the Sutlej–Gobind Sagar system through the 990-MW Dehar hydropower station; Unit-II is Pong Dam.
Pong Dam, Pandoh Dam and the Beas–Sutlej Link form the Beas Project; Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon and Panchet are DVC dams.
Tilaiya, Konar and Maithon belong to the DVC system; Pong belongs to the Beas Project.
The DVC first-stage sequence is Tilaiya–Barakar–1953, Konar–Konar–1955, Maithon–Barakar–1957 and Panchet–Damodar–1959.

pages.source_heading: Register of major Indian multipurpose projects - part 2

facts.claim: Kangsabati is in West Bengal. Mettur is in Tamil Nadu, Rana Pratap Sagar in Rajasthan and Jayakwadi in Maharashtra.
Bansagar–Son, Dulhasti–Chenab and Mettur–Kaveri are all correct; the other chains swap rivers.
Loktak belongs to Manipur's Loktak system, Tehri and Koteshwar are both on the Bhagirathi, and Tapovan–Vishnugad is a hydropower project on the Dhauliganga.
Ranjit Sagar (Thein) is on the Ravi, Malaprabha is on its namesake river, and both Jayakwadi and Vishnupuri belong to the Godavari system in Maharashtra.
Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada in Gujarat, Kangsabati belongs to the Kangsabati–Kumari system in West Bengal, and Mettur/Stanley is on the Kaveri in Tamil Nadu.
Not every printed entry is a dam. Dhuvaran is a thermal power station, Farakka a diversion barrage on the Ganga, and Bisalpur a water-supply and irrigation project on the Banas in Rajasthan.

pages.source_heading: River-water disputes and tribunal chronology

facts.claim: An allocation is a context-dependent legal figure. A printed number should not be called the current entitlement without its dependability, award/report date, gazette or court modification, and later state-reorganisation context.
The Kaveri set is correct. The other options exchange the Vansadhara, Mahadayi and Mahanadi state groups.

KWDT-I was constituted on 10 April 1969 and accepted 2,060 TMC as the 75% dependable flow at Vijayawada. KWDT-II was constituted on 2 April 2004, with 1 February 2006 treated as its effective date by the Supreme Court.
Article 262 empowers Parliament to legislate on inter-state river-water disputes; the operational framework is the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra are the principal states in the Mahadayi/Mandovi basin dispute.

pages.source_heading: Tribunal awards and inter-state projects

facts.claim: The 2007 award allocated 419 TMC to Tamil Nadu, 270 to Karnataka, 30 to Kerala and 7 to Puducherry. The first two values changed in the 2018 Supreme Court modification.
The Supreme Court increased Karnataka's share by 14.75 TMC to 284.75 and reduced Tamil Nadu's by the same amount to 404.25. Kerala remained at 30 and Puducherry at 7 TMC.
The Ravi–Beas Water Tribunal was constituted in 1986, while the official CWC document is the Tribunal Report of 1987. The formation and report years differ.
The Godavari and Narmada tribunals were both constituted in 1969. Godavari's report/final stages were 1979–80, Narmada's award was in 1979, and Ravi–Beas was constituted in 1986 and reported in 1987.
Mahadayi and Vansadhara were both constituted in 2010. Mahadayi's award came in 2018; Vansadhara's final order in 2017 and further report in 2021. The Mahanadi Tribunal was constituted in 2018.

pages.source_heading: Indus Waters Treaty and Indus-basin projects

facts.claim: MEA material states that India and Bangladesh share 54 common rivers. The Joint Rivers Commission is a bilateral mechanism; the book's claim of nine tribunals is wrong.
The Ganga Waters Treaty was signed on 12 December 1996 and governs Ganga water sharing at Farakka during the lean season from 1 January to 31 May.
The treaty defines Eastern and Western river groups and the permitted uses on them. A 20:80 split may be a rough hydrological summary, but it is not the treaty's operational allocation formula.
Kishenganga lies in the Jhelum basin, while Salal, Baglihar, Dulhasti and Ratle are on the Chenab; all belong to the Western Rivers context.
The treaty classifies Ravi, Beas and Sutlej as Eastern Rivers, and Indus, Jhelum and Chenab as Western Rivers.
The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Jawaharlal Nehru for India and Ayub Khan for Pakistan, with World Bank facilitation.
Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are the Eastern Rivers; Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are the Western Rivers.
Kishenganga is a Jhelum tributary, while Salal and Ratle are on the Chenab system.
The Mahakali Treaty integrates Sarada Barrage, Tanakpur Barrage and the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project; the Mahakali is a boundary river along major stretches between India and Nepal.

pages.source_heading: Water-storage and flow-measurement units

facts.claim: A cusec is a cubic foot per second and a cumec a cubic metre per second; therefore 1 cusec is about 0.0283168 m³/s and 1 cumec about 35.3147 cusecs.
About 1,233.48 m³ is one acre-foot. A million acre-feet is about 1.23348 billion m³.
One TMC ft is one billion cubic feet, approximately 28.3168 million cubic metres.

pages.source_heading: Nagarjuna Sagar and Prakasam Barrage

facts.claim: Prakasam Barrage regulates and diverts Krishna water into delta canals; it is not equivalent to a high storage dam.
The printed installed capacity is 966 MW; Jawahar Right Canal is 203 km and Lal Bahadur Left Canal 295 km.
The book gives Nagarjuna Sagar gross storage as 408 TMC, live storage as 312 TMC and FRL as 590 ft. Gross, live and present storage must not be mixed.
AP government material gives a length of 1,233 m, 70 gates, design flood of 11.90 lakh cusecs and storage of 3.071 TMC. The book's 1,223 m length is a typographical error.

facts.claim: Srisailam has an FRL of 885 ft, gross storage of about 216 TMC and combined installed power of 1,670 MW. The current AP realtime gross-capacity figure is about 215.79 TMC.

pages.source_heading: Gundlakamma, Guru Raghavendra, Handri-Neeva, Pulichintala, Telugu Ganga and Polavaram

facts.claim: The printed Gundlakamma figures are 3.2 TMC and 80,060 acres. Guru Raghavendra lifts 5.40 TMC from TBLLC for 50,000 acres in nine mandals.

HNSS lifts 40 TMC from Srisailam at Malyala for Rayalaseema. Veligonda conveys Krishna water through tunnels to Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa; printed targets are 43.5 TMC, 4.5 lakh acres and 15 lakh people.

Pulichintala/K. L. Rao Sagar is a Krishna balancing reservoir, printed at 45.75 TMC and 120 MW. Tarakarama Lift is on the Budameru, with printed targets of 56,000 acres, 64 villages, eight mandals and 3 TMC.

pages.source_heading: Polavaram project specifications and allocation issues

facts.claim: MW is a unit of power capacity. Storage is stated in TMC, canal length in kilometres and energy generation in MWh or GWh.
PPA specifies 960 MW as 12×80 MW, 48 radial gates, drinking water for 28.5 lakh people in 611 villages, and rim-sharing of 5 TMC with Odisha and 1.5 TMC with Chhattisgarh.
The PPA gives the Left Main Canal as 181.999 km, the Right Main Canal as 178.810 km and diversion to the Krishna basin as 80 TMC. The 75.2-TMC figure is live capacity at FRL +45.72 m.
The printed table gives 178.8 km, 212.3 km and 960 MW respectively; storage and utilisation are distinct metrics.
